problem: Whether V δD, the product of variance and the normalized Turán-inequality deficit at the first descent of a Poisson-binomial pmf, admits a universal lower bound.
gap: Existing bounds on log-concavity deficits either depend on the number of summands, degenerate under certain conditions, or do not directly control the Turán deficit δD.
contribution: Proof that V δD ≥ 1/4 for variance V ≥ 1, establishing that the infimum of V δD lies between 1/4 and 1/3, with applications to polynomial coefficient sequences.
note: Novel bound with gap between 1/4 and 1/3 that reviewers will assess for proof rigor and optimality of the constant.
